items.title: The booming cash advance industry trapping America’s small businesses
items.summary: What would you do if a financial deal you believed was a lifeline blew up your life? When a California entrepreneur landed in the world of merchant cash advances, he found America’s fastest-growing — and least regulated — source of funding for small businesses. Its daily payments and broken promises left him a changed man, back in his teenage bedroom, over $5 million in debt. NPR business correspondent Alina Selyukh joins The Sunday Story to trace his stubborn battle against an industry where borrowers rarely fight back.

items.title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
items.summary: Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report. In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund ( UNFPA ) published on Thursday.
items.body: One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.

items.title: European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt
items.summary: Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi. The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen , the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.

items.title: ‘Weak and dizzy’: the secretive ICE force-feeding tactics that ended a Cuban father’s hunger strike
items.summary: Exclusive: Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez says in messages to Guardian from inside Texas facility pain of force-feeding caused him to break strike The text message that came from inside the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention center was stark: “I have spent five days eating regular food. If I don’t eat it, they put the tube in me to feed me.” A Cuban asylum seeker, Luis Alejandro Cora Pérez, 32, said in messages to the Guardian this month that he was still weak and dizzy after three months without eating, but that he had broken his hunger strike because being force-fed was just too painful.

items.body: Mairzy Doates (April 1, 1976 – May 25, 1998) was an American Thoroughbred racehorse and multiple graded stakes winner, most remembered for her victory at the inaugural Japan Cup in 1981. Owned by New York City art dealer Arno D. Schefler and trained primarily by future U.S. Racing Hall of Fame inductee Horatio Luro, she competed successfully across the United States from 1978 to 1981, including winning the Yerba Buena Handicap twice. In her final race, she traveled to Tokyo to contest the first Japan Cup, an international invitational established by the Japan Racing Association (JRA) to assess Japanese horses' performance against the rest of the world. She defeated the field in a course-record time, which alongside the strength of the other foreign horses, was widely considered as evidence of the disparity between Japanese and international horse-racing standards. Her performance is frequently credited as the catalyst for the JRA's long-term initiative to improve the caliber of Japanese breeding and racing. Following her victory, which made her 1981's highest earning mare globally, Mairzy Doates retired from racing to become a broodmare in Midway, Kentucky. She gave birth to nine foals before dying at the age of 22. == Early life == Mairzy Doates was born April 1, 1976, bred by Preston and Patrick Madden, a pair of horse-training brothers who operated out of Hamburg Place in Kentucky. Her sire was Nodouble, a multiple graded stakes winner who had retired to stud in 1970, and later became the leading sire in North America in 1981. In contrast, her dam, Avalanche Lily, had only raced lightly and never won, but she was a foal of leading sire and 1960 Grass Horse of the Year T. V. Lark, and a descendant of Man o' War. Mairzy Doates's mare line traces directly to Cinq a Sept, winner of the 1927 Irish Oaks, making Mairzy Doates a distant relative of Secretariat. Two years later in 1978, Arno D. Schefler, a New York art dealer and investment banker who had dealt in Thoroughbred horses since 1967, purchased Mairzy Doates as a filly from the Maddens. Schefler was the one to name her, referencing the novelty song "Mairzy Doats" made popular in a 1943 recording by bandleader Al Trace. She was briefly trained by Angel Penna and then Mickey Preger, but by winter, Schefler had handed Mairzy Doates over to Horatio Luro, a veteran horse-trainer with whom Schefler had become acquainted in the early 1970s. Mairzy Doates was brought to Luro's stable in Miami, where she had to be closely monitored while training due to the weakness of her ankles. == Racing history == Mairzy Doates raced once as a two-year-old, finishing sixth out of ten at the Aqueduct Racetrack on December 22, 1978. Over two months, Mairzy Doates vied several times for a maiden race victory, eventually winning on her fourth attempt on February 4, 1979.
